mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates a slack labor market, which typically precedes a recovery in consumer demand and corporate investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between industrial production (INDPRO) and capacity utilization (implied by INDPRO relative to historical peaks) signals underutilized capacity despite moderate output growth, which typically precedes a supply-side catch-up and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA but < 80% of 5-year peak for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
